findings.title: Missing re-check of the cache after acquiring the write lock (double-checked locking)
findings.body: After taking the exclusive lock, GetWebAssets does not re-check whether another goroutine already populated entryPointAssetsCache. At startup (or whenever the cache is empty), every concurrent request observes a nil cache under the read lock, then queues on the write lock; each one in turn re-reads and re-parses assets-manifest.json from disk (or fetches it over HTTP if the CDN path at line 56 is ever enabled) and overwrites the cache, with all but the last result discarded. This is the standard double-checked-locking pattern with the second check missing. Adding `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` immediately after acquiring the write lock avoids the redundant serialized I/O.

findings.title: Exclusive lock held across manifest I/O serializes all callers
findings.body: The write lock acquired at line 48 is held (via defer) for the entire recompute, including the disk read of assets-manifest.json and, if enabled, the CDN HTTP fetch. While any writer holds it, all other callers block on the initial RLock at line 41. In dev mode the cache is deliberately bypassed on every call, so every request to GetWebAssets is now serialized through this single global mutex plus a disk read. The same happens in non-dev mode whenever the manifest read persistently fails, because the cache then stays nil and every request retries under the exclusive lock, turning a missing-file misconfiguration into a global serialization point for index page loads. Consider doing the read outside the lock and taking the write lock only to publish the result (combined with the re-check from the previous point).

findings.title: Race fix ships without a regression test exercising concurrent access
findings.body: This PR fixes a data race on the global entryPointAssetsCache but adds no test. Nothing guards the new synchronization: if someone later removes the mutex or accesses the global without it, nothing in the test suite would catch it. A simple test that calls GetWebAssets from many goroutines (against a temp assets-manifest.json) and is run under `go test -race` would fail if the synchronization regresses and would document the concurrency contract of this function.
